title: Oyster Mushroom Asada
cScaleSummary: Oyster mushrooms, citrus, garlic, herbs, and spices provide bold flavor with essentially no dietary cholesterol and very little saturated fat.
ldlActiveSummary: While highly cholesterol-conscious, this recipe does not contain a significant source of soluble fiber or other ingredients with established LDL-lowering effects.
intro: Oyster mushrooms naturally shred and char, making them an excellent stand-in for traditional carne asada. A citrus-garlic marinade, smoky spices, chipotle, and a hot cast-iron skillet create deeply savory flavor and crisp edges that are perfect for tacos, bowls, or burritos.

stepGroups.title: Instructions
items: Tear the 1 pound oyster mushrooms into bite-sized strips, leaving some larger pieces for texture.

Whisk together the 3 tablespoons lime juice, 2 tablespoons orange juice, 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 3 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1 minced chipotle pepper in adobo.
Toss the 1 pound oyster mushrooms with the marinade until evenly coated. Let stand for 20 to 30 minutes.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add the 1 tablespoon olive oil and swirl to coat the skillet.
Add the marinated oyster mushrooms and all of the marinade to the skillet.
Cook undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes to develop deep browning and char.
Stir the mushrooms and continue cooking for 6 to 8 minutes until the liquid evaporates and the mushrooms become dark, concentrated, and crispy around the edges.
Continue cooking as needed until patches of char appear across the mushrooms.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro.
Serve the oyster mushroom carne asada in the warm tortillas topped with the 1/2 cup finely diced white onion, 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, and lime wedges.
